title: Evaluation of Surfactant Extracted from Asparagus nelsii Schinz Roots in Detergent Formulation
content: The rising demand for eco-friendly personal care products has prompted the exploration of bio-surfactants, derived from renewable sources, as sustainable alternatives to synthetic surfactants in detergent formulations. This study investigated the extraction, characterization, and evaluation of surfactant properties from Asparagus nelsii Schinz, a plant native to southern Africa and tradi-tionally valued for its medicinal properties and high foaming ability. The extraction process in-volved isolating saponin-based compounds from the roots of A. nelsii, known for their amphiphilic characteristics that facilitate effective surfactant behaviour. Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy analysis revealed key functional groups, including hydroxyl, carbonyl, and alkyl chains, indicating the biosurfactant’s amphiphilic structure essential for surface tension reduction and emulsification. Comparative analysis with synthetic sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) highlighted the biosurfactant’s strong surface-active properties, showing greater surface-tension reduction at lower concentrations, which is advantageous for formulations that deliver mild yet effective cleansing. Emulsification index testing further demonstrated its ability to stabilize vegetable oil emulsions, suggesting potential use in natural personal care products that require stable emul-sions. Performance assessments of the formulated detergent demonstrated effective cleansing ability, with the biosurfactant achieving consistent lather formation and foam stability over time.
